The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighLatency on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: p95 latency above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-10T23:19:05Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-10T23:19:27Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came 6 minutes 5 seconds {detection_gap} after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
Broken from 2026-11-10T23:12:00Z {began} (the onset) to 2026-11-10T23:21:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 9 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 3 minutes 43 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-10T23:23:09Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 0.6% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 1.5% {errors_at_worst} - no higher than the worst minutes of stretches as long before it began.
Rise above baseline: none - no more of the traffic failed while it was broken than before it began.
The series behind the alert, `max(http_request_duration_seconds{quantile="0.95"}) * 1000` - its alert said "p95 latency above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 215.23333333333332 ms {series_before} before it began, 1434.2222222222222 ms {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 1722 ms {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
No rise in failed requests was measured, so the harm to report is what this series did: say what it meant for the people using the service, not that little or nothing failed.
Customer loss: none - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-10T23:19:25Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighLatency on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-10T23:19:42Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-10T23:19:43Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-10T23:19:50Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 23:19:05 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-10T23:19:54Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-10T23:19:55Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 23:12 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-10T23:19:55Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-10T23:19:56Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 10 23:13 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-10T23:19:57Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-10T23:19:57Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
  - [T11] 2026-11-10T23:19:57Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 37 {T11.2} minutes 5 {T11.3} seconds before 23:19:05 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-10T23:19:58Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 103 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-10T23:19:59Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-10T23:19:59Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-10T23:19:59Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 23:19:59 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-10T23:20:03Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-10T23:20:04Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-10T23:20:04Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Restarted io-pricing, a dependency of io-shop for C1
  - [T19] 2026-11-10T23:20:12Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 23:21 {T19.2} - up to 234s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-10T23:23:09Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 23:20 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-10T23:23:09Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-10T23:23:09Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - restarted [io-pricing] and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-10T23:25:15Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/523

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 57 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 38 {G46bc.2} minutes, 22:42–23:19 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 35 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 38 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 22:42–23:19 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 3.00% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 22:50 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 3 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 18 {Gad41.2} minutes, 22:59–23:16 {Gad41.3}
  - [G9feb] WARN io-shop: slow upstream call - pricing.io-internal.svc took 1500ms {G9feb.1} for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/basket-total (# of 200 {G9feb.2} requests) - 8 {G9feb.3} occurrences in 8 {G9feb.4} minutes, 23:12–23:19 {G9feb.5}; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/basket-total took 8 {G9feb.6} different values; # was 43 {G9feb.7} to 200 {G9feb.8}, typically 200 {G9feb.9}, highest at 23:13 {G9feb.10}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] io-pricing, an internal service owned by checkout-platform, began taking about 1500ms {C1.1} per basket-total call at 23:12 {C1.2}. The account page waits on it, so p50, p95 and p99 all jumped. io-shop itself is healthy: nothing was deployed or changed, and CPU, memory and error rate are flat. [internal-dependency-failure, confidence 0.9 {C1.3}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Restarted io-pricing for [C1] - confirmed, nothing to put back

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: the basket total is optional. The account page already shows without it when pricing gives no price, because `_the_basket_for` catches `PricingServiceFailed`. But `basket_total` set no limit on how long it would wait for an answer. When io-pricing started taking 1500ms {F1.1}, every account page waited the full 1500ms {F1.2}, and io-shop's p50 went from 45ms {F1.3} to about 1546ms {F1.4}. io-shop did no retrying, fell back on nothing and never gave up. It just wrote a log line about how slow the call was and kept waiting. So someone else's slowdown became io-shop's latency in full, for something the page can do without.
      
      The fix, all in `pricing_service.basket_total`:
      - A new limit, `PRICING_BUDGET_MS = 300`. The normal call is around 12ms {F1.5}, and the existing warning threshold is 200ms {F1.6}.
      - The call now runs on a small worker pool, and the code waits for it with `future.result(timeout=...)`. A call that hangs or crawls is given up on after the limit, whatever the network does.
      - If the service reports that the call took longer than the limit, that also counts as running out of time. The service is reached through a function the caller passes in, and that function reports how long the call took.
      - Either way, `PricingServiceFailed` is raised with a message naming the host, the path and the limit. The account page already catches that and renders the page with "Pricing is not available right now", keeping the message as `pricing_failure`.
      
      Nothing is hidden: errors other than running out of time still pass through unchanged, a no-price answer still fails the same way, and calls between 200ms {F1.7} and 300ms {F1.8} still return a price and are still reported as slow. `account_page.py` doesn't need to change because it already treats `PricingServiceFailed` as "show the page without the basket".
      
      Tests:
      - A service that answers in 1500ms {F1.9} now leaves the page without its basket total. The old code returned the price, so this test fails against it.
      - A service that blocks for real is given up on well within a second. The old code waited the whole time, so this test fails against it too.
      - Calls that are slow but within the limit still return a price and a slow-call line.
      - The two tests that expected a 1500ms {F1.10} answer to come back as a price now describe the new behaviour instead.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus:
  - [U1] basket_total at src/io_shop/account_page.py:183, in _the_basket_for: calls it: return basket_total(shopper_id, ask_the_pricing_service), None
  - Where [F1] says otherwise of these lines, they stand.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Restarted io-pricing
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #523 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: basket_total, which _the_basket_for calls to fetch the account page's optional basket total, sets no limit on how long it waits for io-pricing, so when io-pricing's basket-total calls began taking {G9feb.1}, every account page waited out the whole call. The page's existing fallback, which renders it without the total, only runs on PricingServiceFailed, and a slow answer never raises that. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: A pricing service the shop asks for each shopper's basket total began answering slowly, and the shop's account pages likely waited for it with no time limit, even though they can be shown without that total.
still_at_risk: If io-pricing slows down again, every account page could again slow down by the same amount.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly. The latency of io-shop's slowest requests rose past the alert's line and stayed there until the alert fired. (cites AL1)
causal_chain 2: From the onset, io-shop's calls to io-pricing for each shopper's basket total took {G9feb.1} each, logged as slow upstream calls over {G9feb.5}. The slowness came from io-pricing, the internal service owned by checkout-platform. (cites G9feb, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order"; T22, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: Each account page waited for that call to finish. _the_basket_for calls basket_total on the page's path, and basket_total sets no limit on how long it waits, so a slow answer was waited out in full instead of failing over to the page's existing fallback without the total. (cites U1, under "How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main by Argus"; F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: No review or test check was seen that requires calls from io-shop to its dependencies to have a time limit. Code-Fix's reading says io-shop's existing tests expected a slow pricing answer to come back as a price.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The unbounded wait on io-pricing would have been flagged before the code shipped, and a slow io-pricing would have left account pages without the basket total instead of slowing them.
contributing_factors 2: io-pricing's slowdown was found only by io-shop's latency alert. No alert on io-pricing's own latency was seen, and nothing was seen alerting on the slow-upstream-call warnings io-shop logged from the onset.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The slowdown would have been flagged at its source, pointing straight at io-pricing and its owners, without having to work back from io-shop's latency.
action_items 1: Add a review or lint check requiring every outbound call from io-shop to a dependency to set a time limit.
action_items 2: Add a latency alert on io-pricing's basket-total endpoint, owned by checkout-platform.
action_items 3: Add an alert on the rate of io-shop's slow-upstream-call warnings for each dependency.
action_items 4: Have checkout-platform find out why io-pricing's basket-total calls slowed down and what restarting it cleared.
action_items 5: Route io-shop's HighLatency alert to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
